people.name: Harshavardhana
people.significance: Consolidated northern India with capital at Kannauj; patron of Nalanda University and author of Sanskrit plays; chronicled by Banabhatta and Xuanzang.
people.chapter: Chapter 3: Empires and Kingdoms: 6th to 10th Centuries

people.name: Pulakeshin II
people.significance: Defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada River; recorded in the Aihole inscription composed by court poet Ravikirti.
people.chapter: Chapter 3: Empires and Kingdoms: 6th to 10th Centuries

people.name: Rajendra I
people.significance: Conducted a historic naval expedition across the Bay of Bengal to conquer Srivijaya ports and secure maritime Indian Ocean trade routes.

people.name: Mahmud of Ghazni
people.significance: Executed 17 military raids into northern India in the early 11th century targeting rich temple cities (including Somnath in 1026 CE) for wealth plunder.

people.name: Muhammad Ghuri
people.significance: Fought the Battles of Tarain (1191 & 1192 CE) against Prithviraj Chauhan, winning the second battle and establishing Turkic territorial power in Delhi.

people.name: Al-Biruni
people.significance: Accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni, mastered Sanskrit, studied Hindu astronomical and mathematical texts, and authored 'Kitab al-Hind'.

people.name: Bhaskaracharya II
people.significance: Composed 'Lilavati' and 'Siddhanta Shiromani' in Sanskrit verse, advancing algebra, geometry, permutations, and planetary motion equations.

people.name: King Jadi Rana
people.significance: Granted sanctuary and religious freedom to 8th-century Parsi Zoroastrian refugees fleeing persecution in Persia.
people.chapter: Chapter 5: India, a Home to Many

people.name: Hirabai Lobi
people.significance: Founded self-help groups and organic farming networks for Siddi tribal women in Gujarat; awarded Padma Shri in 2023.
people.chapter: Chapter 5: India, a Home to Many

cause_effect.cause: Heavy tropical rainfall in regions like the Western Ghats and Meghalaya causes intense leaching of topsoil.
cause_effect.effect: Formation of acidic, iron-rich Laterite soil, which is ideal for cashew, tea, coffee, and rubber plantations.
cause_effect.chapter: Chapter 1: The Story of Indian Farming

cause_effect.cause: Excessive tube-well pumping of underground aquifers for flood irrigation in arid zones.
cause_effect.effect: Groundwater tables drop drastically and soil salinity increases as evaporated water leaves a salty crust.
cause_effect.chapter: Chapter 1: The Story of Indian Farming

cause_effect.cause: Strategic position of Kannauj commanding trade routes and Gangetic agricultural revenue.
cause_effect.effect: Triggered the centuries-long Tripartite Struggle between Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas, and Rashtrakutas.
cause_effect.chapter: Chapter 3: Empires and Kingdoms: 6th to 10th Centuries

cause_effect.cause: Chola Emperor Rajendra I launched a blue-water naval campaign across the Bay of Bengal.
cause_effect.effect: Defeated Srivijaya empire, securing Indian Ocean maritime trade routes connecting South India with China and Southeast Asia.

cause_effect.cause: Destruction of centralized monastic universities like Nalanda during 12th-century military incursions.
cause_effect.effect: Manuscript archives were lost, forcing scholars to disperse to Nepal/Tibet and decentralize scholarly transmission into regional courts and family math schools.

cause_effect.cause: Parsed interest compounding where interest is calculated on accumulated prior interest.
cause_effect.effect: Savings grow exponentially over long tenures, whereas unpaid debt compounds into destructive debt traps.
cause_effect.chapter: Chapter 8: Banks and the Magic of Finance
